answer: Daily pay would require each ecology agent to label 20 disjoint, balanced images of lagoon pollution, glacier melt or cedar disease, with at least 18 correct. Auditors grade against hidden labels; validators check signed key/day passes and single-use image IDs. Missing or failed checks deny pay. Thus n keys need 20n labels/day; parallelism cuts time, not task count. Inference is recurring work; GPUs are reusable capital. Shared models can make Sybils profitable; corrupt auditors can forge passes. This assumes fresh images, not reusable answer banks; it does not prove distinct owners.
